findings.failure_path: The recommended skipLibCheck:true baseline also skips first-party declarations, including the hand-written types/ declarations recommended by modules-and-publishing.md. A declaration such as `export const value: MissingType` can therefore pass the compiler gate despite an unresolved type. The warning against intentionally hiding errors does not prevent this automatic false green.
findings.smallest_fix: Require skipLibCheck:false in the verification gate for first-party and published declarations; make the performance option conditional on that separate check.

findings.failure_path: The replacement drops 'No any in shipped code.' The destination reference permits first-party any with a reason and narrow scope. An agent can now ship an any-typed component callback or internal helper under that exception, although the previous React contract prohibited it. Preserving unknown at API boundaries does not preserve this separate obligation.
findings.smallest_fix: Retain the React prohibition on shipped any alongside the boundary pointer, or preserve an equally strong obligation in the destination reference.
